# Laravel Orphan Files (`erag/laravel-orphan-files`)

> Finds files on Laravel disks (local, public, S3, and S3-compatible storage such as MinIO and RustFS) that no database row references, and moves them to a trash folder that can be restored. Artisan commands only; no migrations, no UI.

## Links

## Install
```bash
composer require erag/laravel-orphan-files
php artisan orphan:install
```
`orphan:install` creates `config/orphan-files.php`, asks before overwriting an existing one (`--force` skips the question) and prints the next steps. It never touches the database.

## Commands
- `php artisan orphan:install` creates `config/orphan-files.php` and prints the next steps.
- `php artisan orphan:scan` reports files, references, orphans and reclaimable size. Read-only. Excluded paths are skipped and not counted.
- `php artisan orphan:clean` is a dry run; `--force` moves orphans to `.orphan-trash/{disk}/{date}/`; `--mode=delete` deletes them for good. A forced clean stops (exit code 1) when more than `max_orphan_ratio` (90%) of a disk would go.
- `php artisan orphan:restore {path}` moves trashed files back to their original path, looking in the trash of every configured disk unless `--disk` is given. `--list` shows the trash, `--all` restores everything.
- `php artisan orphan:purge-trash` deletes trash older than `trash.retention_days` (30) on every disk, for good. `--days=N` keeps the last N days, `--all` removes everything, `--dry-run` only counts.
- `php artisan orphan:explain {path}` shows which rows reference a file, or why it is kept, excluded or an orphan. Read-only.

## Rules for agents
Always run a scan or a dry run first and show the result. Never use `--force`, `--mode=delete`, `--force-ratio` or `orphan:purge-trash` without the user's approval. Never lower `grace_period_hours` without asking.
